name: Goddess movement
summary: The Goddess movement is a non-centralized religious current, rooted in second-wave feminism, that worships a female divine or the divine as immanent in nature, the body and women's lives. Its leading voices, Carol Christ and Starhawk, reject patriarchal religion and its male God as a legitimation of male power, tie the domination of women to the domination of nature, hold the sacred to be in nature and the person, and favour nonhierarchical community and nonviolent change. It has no programme on economics, the state or foreign policy, so most statements are unanswered.
scope: The feminist Goddess spirituality of the 1970s onward as set out by its founding thinkers Carol P. Christ (Why Women Need the Goddess, with Judith Plaskow) and Starhawk (The Spiral Dance); the reference works describe the movement as a non-centralized trend with no tenets common to every adherent, so only positions these thinkers state as the movement's own count. Covens, Reclaiming and other organizations, and Dianic or other strands as bodies, are not used as sources.
